newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 rebounds but dealers ask, will it last?.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 rebounds but dealers ask, will it last?.

text.p: The Czech PX50 rebounded on Wednesday with the three most heavily weighted shares on the index posting solid gains.
The PX50 closed up 3.4 points, 0.6 percent, to 556.7, a rare upward sessions on an index which has dropped by 11 percent since posting a two year high of 629 on February 26.
Despite Wednesday's gains, dealers hestitated to predict a sustained uptrend and said much depended on foreign investors.
"It depends on the international situation. If stock prices are not supported by international investors here they start to fall," said Pavel Sobisek of Zivnostenska Banka.
"Whether this is going to be the beginning of a trend, I don't know," added Jiri Susicky of Patria Finance.
Major issues, which have bourne the brunt of recent declines, were at the forefront of the rebound.
SPT Telecom gained 41 crowns, 1.2 percent, to 3,440, CEZ rose 29 crowns, 2.8 percent, to 1,060 and Komercni Banka was up 64 crowns, 2.7 percent, to 2,430.
Together, the three issues account for 45 percent of the PX50's capitalisation.
Overall, turnover was 974 million crowns and volume was 1,028,837 shares.
